bull.b: Progression into the highest planned dose cohort, alongside full enrollment of the 10 mg/kg cohort, indicates PepGen is advancing a meaningful clinical program. Upcoming data and planned regulatory engagement could provide important evidence for the platform’s therapeutic potential.

The reported cash position and projected runway into the fourth quarter of 2027 give PepGen time to generate clinical data without an immediately necessary financing event. That liquidity supports continued development and reduces near-term execution pressure.

Lower research and development spending and a narrower quarterly loss suggest some improvement in cost management while the pipeline continues advancing. If sustained, this could moderate the rate of capital consumption and extend the company’s ability to fund development.

bear.b: PepGen remains entirely dependent on clinical development because it has no approved commercial products or recurring product revenue. Until a program reaches commercialization or a material partnership generates income, operating progress is unlikely to translate into self-sustaining revenue.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow shows that PepGen’s current activities are not self-funding. Even with burn improving from earlier periods, continued investment in trials will require substantial liquidity and leaves the company reliant on external financing over time.

The declining equity base reflects the cumulative effect of ongoing losses and reduces the capital cushion available to support development. Deeply negative returns on equity also indicate that shareholder capital is not yet producing economic returns, increasing funding pressure if losses persist.
